loci.rationale: Access route: owner-only check (who==c['owner'], 403 otherwise), store.access call, JSON attachment delivery with no-store header.
Session identity resolution from cookie; establishes 'who' used for authorization and owner scoping.
get_case scopes the single case by id AND (owner=? OR officer=?), preventing cross-applicant case retrieval.
access() assembles the copy: case row (supplied/derived fields), NOTICE processing information, events and jobs by cid, preferences by case owner only.
NOTICE text supplied as processing_information in the access copy.
Automatic decision event (derived decision) recorded per cid and surfaced in the timeline.
Partner source event (Income Registry band) recorded per cid and surfaced in the timeline.
Human review decision event recorded per cid, included in the access timeline.

output.path_summary: GET /case/<cid>/access is handled in app.py: the session user is resolved from the cookie (app.py:0044-0047), the case is fetched via store.get_case which filters by id AND (owner=? OR officer=?) (store.py:0055-0058), the access branch requires who==c['owner'] (app.py:0105) and calls store.access(db,c) (app.py:0106), returning JSON as an attachment with no-store (app.py:0030, 0107-0109). store.access builds the copy from the single case row, events WHERE cid=?, jobs WHERE cid=?, and choices WHERE owner=c['owner'] (store.py:0118-0122), embedding NOTICE (store.py:0009) and the timeline that carries partner-notice and decision events (store.py:0135, 0160, 0196). Isolation of the other applicant is structural: per-cid and per-owner queries, no cross-case join.
missing_boundaries: No runtime execution or observation was performed; assessment is static reading of the supplied snapshot only.
The scenario's 'verified borrower' status is not modeled as a separate verification flag; it is treated as the authenticated owner session.
Completeness of the copy for every derived field (e.g., summaries.title, receiver payloads, confirmed band provenance) is not asserted beyond the fields enumerated in store.access.
No third-party-rights redaction mechanism exists; isolation relies on per-cid/per-owner queries rather than redaction.
No conclusion is drawn about other GDPR articles or about upstream/other versions of the code.
